question.leadin: Give the following about a French religious group.
question.text: The Edict of Saint-Germain was passed by Queen Catherine de Medici in 1572. It guaranteed private worship by this group of French Protestants.
question.clue: These people were welcomed into Prussia via the Edict of Potsdam.

swap.leadin: The Treaty of Verdun divided this man's lands between Lothair, Charles the Bald, and Louis the German.
swap.text: Name this son of Pepin the Short, a Frankish king who conquered much of Western Europe.
swap.answerHtml: Charlemagne [or Charles I or Charles the Great; or Carolus Magnus; prompt on Charles]
swap.clue: One of this man's sons, whom he made King of Italy, was initially named after his possibly-murdered brother Carloman, and the scholar Alcuin of York reformed handwriting at this man's Palace School.

question.text: This leader of the Second French Empire was captured by the Prussians at the Battle of Sedan. He shares his name with his uncle, an earlier French emperor.
question.clue: Another satire suggests that this ruler combined Heinrich Heine's character Crapulinski with the "holy phalanx of order" by installing himself as a "savior of society" with the support of the underclasses or lumpen.

swap.leadin: This period during the French Revolution was sparked by the promulgation of the Law of Suspects.
swap.text: Name this time during the French Revolution when thousands of "enemies of the Revolution," including Marie Antoinette, were guillotined.
swap.clue: It was marked by legislation like the Law of Suspects and by incidents like the noyades, where priests and nuns were tied together and drowned.

question.text: The French agents demanded that a bribe of $250,000 be given to this French foreign minister who served under Napoleon and represented France at the Congress of Vienna.
question.clue: He was critical of the harsh provisions imposed on Prussia and Austria in the Treaties of Tilsit and Pressburg, and fell out of favor in the later part of Napoleon's reign.

swap.text: Cardinal Mazarin also put down this 1648 uprising of the nobility which was precipitated after the Peace of Westphalia. The participants wanted to call the Estates General.
swap.clue: Divided into parts named for the Parliament and the Nobles, it occurred during the regency of Anne of Austria.

question.text: This minister of finance under Louis helped produce the economic base to finance Louis's wars. He's known for his mercantilist policies, and he reduced the number of nobles exempt from tax.
question.clue: His predecessor was Nicolas Fouquet, who was charged with embezzlement due to the charges brought about by this man.

swap.text: This French peasant's revolt occurred during the 100 Year's war following the imposition of a series of particularly onerous taxes, and saw largely unorganized attacks against the nobility.
swap.clue: A one-sided battle at Mello crushed its organized military wing after its main leader, Guillame Cale, was murdered at a parlay with Charles the Bad and the Mayor of Paris, Etienne Marcel, was killed for lending tacit support to it.

question.leadin: Identify the following about the Nueva Planta decrees.
question.text: In response, the Aragonese backed this Holy Roman Emperor over the French candidate for the Spanish throne. This emperor issued the Pragmatic Sanction to pass on his territories to Maria Theresa. Give his title as Holy Roman Emperor.
question.answerHtml: Charles VI [or Karl VI; do not accept or prompt on "Charles II" or "Charles III" as he wasn't called that as Holy Roman Emperor]
question.clue: A later king with this name won the Burgundians over to his side with the Treaty of Arras and was crowned in 1429 thanks to Joan of Arc.

swap.text: This dynasty lends its name to a variant of Latin script used in many 8th century manuscripts. This dynasty was founded by Clovis I in 509.
swap.clue: These kings all had long hair and gave power to regional "mayors of the palace" after Dagobert I's rule.

question.text: The Popular Front organized the Million Franc Race to encourage competition with German automobile manufacturers, which was eventually won by a man with this last name. A man with this last name was opposed by La Libre Parole and imprisoned on Devil's Island.

swap.text: This monk is popularly, but wrongly, credited with the invention of the traditional method, since they were actually attempting to stop the second fermentation in their wines. This does not prevent Moet et Chandon from naming one of their wines after them.
swap.clue: This French Benedictine monk is often miscredited for the invention of champagne in the 17th century. Regardless, he names a high-sought after brand of champagne sold by Moet & Chandon.

question.leadin: Andrew Israel Ross's Public City/Public Sex explores urban homosexuality during this historiographical period, when Liane de Pougy became a demi-monde icon at the Folies Bergere ("faw-lee bair-zhair").
question.text: Identify this period discussed "beyond Paris" in Dominique Kalifa's cultural history. The Second Industrial Revolution modernized this period of high-society frivolity from Haussman's remodeling of Paris to World War I.
question.answerHtml: La Belle Époque (“eh-POCK”) [prompt on fin de siècle or turn-of-the-century or the late 19th century; prompt on Third Republic or Troisième République; prompt on translations like “beautiful era”]
question.clue: This period of peace and modernization in French history from 1871 to 1914, the name of which literally means "Beautiful Era."

swap.text: De Gaulle was the first president of the French republic of this number.
swap.clue: Mitterrand, like Georges Pompidou and Charles de Gaulle, presided over this republican government of France, which came into being in 1958 and is still around today under Nicolas Sarkozy.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the "history of mentalities," a genre that examines trends in attitudes of ordinary people.
question.text: The genre of "history of mentalities" was popularized by Marc Bloch, the founder of this French school of historiography. Its "second generation" included Fernand Braudel.

swap.text: This prime minister sparked the Rhine Crisis by declaring the river was the "natural eastern border" of France. As the first president of the Third Republic, he ordered Patrice MacMahon to crush the Paris Commune.
swap.clue: The Paris Commune that formed after the war was suppressed by this French leader, who then founded the Third Republic and served as the first president from 1871-1873.

question.leadin: Examples of this policy included the creation of public schools and a law giving city councils control of places of worship.
question.text: Give this French term, used to denote the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Republic's policies of strict separation of church and state.
question.clue: With Emile Combes, Briand was one of the main proponents and authors of a 1905 law that officially implemented this doctrine. The Jules Ferry laws on schooling are the first notable implementation of this doctrine.

swap.leadin: The 1973 oil crisis forced this project to create the pioneering electric Zebulon prototype within a year, and it was part of the "champion national" projects along with the Ariane 1 rocket and the Concorde jet.
swap.text: Name this flagship project of Valery Giscard d'Estaing's ("vah-lay-REE zhee-SCAR day-STAN") administration. Inspired by the Shinkansen, this public transportation project created the TVM signaling mechanism and also exports the Acela trains to the US.
swap.answerHtml: TGV (“tay-zhay-vay”) [or Trains à Grande Vitesse; accept LGV (“ell-zhay-vay”) or Lignes à Grande Vitesse; accept just High-Speed train/rail system since that’s literally what the name means; prompt on just trains or rail and equivalents]

question.text: The father of all commentary on Lamentations, as with the Tanach as a whole, is this 11th and 12th Century French Rabbi.

swap.leadin: After the arrival of General Custine, Caroline Schelling and Georg Forster founded one of these groups in Mainz.
swap.text: British agents feared that "citizen" Tipu Sultan had founded what sort of group in Mysore? The original one of these groups met on the Rue Saint-Honore ("sant on-oh-RAY").
swap.answerHtml: Jacobin clubs [or Clubs des Jacobins; prompt on Jacobins or revolutionary clubs]
